1 رَتِلَ الثَّغْرُ , aor.
رَتَلَ , inf. n. رَتَلٌ, The front teeth were, or became, even in their growth, (Msb,) [or separate, one from another, and even in the manner of growth, well set together, and (accord. to some) very white and lustrous: see رَتَلٌ and رَتِلٌ, below.] ―
-b2- And رَتِلَ الشَّىْءُ, aor. and inf. n. as above, The thing was, or became, well arranged or disposed. (TK.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
